upstream.scope: Resident memory as one defined read-only metric beside PID and name, with explicit unavailable states; no sorting, no further memory fields, no proportional or shared-page accounting, no process controls, no htop parity claim

entries.feature: Resident memory is published as a third table column, stored as an exact u64 byte count and converted once on the server into IEC multiples with the fraction truncated rather than rounded, so a count just below a multiple is never displayed as the multiple it never reached and a value too large for a float is still published exactly
entries.scope: PX-005/fake, scripted and live procfs sources/read-only

entries.feature: A metric definition states the interface the number is read from (/proc/<pid>/stat field 24 in pages, times the page size the scanned mount reports through AT_PAGESZ) and what it does not account for: shared pages counted in full for every mapper, swapped-out and never-faulted pages not counted, and the kernel's own inaccuracy caveat
entries.scope: PX-005/metric definition only; the metric registry, scheduling and availability model are PX-042

entries.feature: Every cell carries its own availability: a resident value the scan could not read is published as Unavailable, or Denied when a permission refused it, never as zero, while a genuine zero stays 0 B; a record whose metric is unreadable is still a published record, so an unreadable field does not make the record list incomplete or add a clause to the status line

The page size is read from the scanned mount's own auxiliary vector rather than from this machine, refused when it is not a believable power of two, and the conversion is checked, so a mount that cannot state a page size publishes no resident value instead of attributing another host's page size or a wrapped product to records never measured under it

On a real Linux host a bounded allocation owned by the test moves the published resident value within a documented tolerance, and the collector's byte count agrees within tolerance with the kernel's own VmRSS for the same process, which the kernel reports in kibibytes and therefore witnesses the page-size conversion independently
entries.scope: PX-005/live procfs source/read-only; tolerances rather than byte equality, because live accounting is not a contract
